$comment: The Slack bot's whole permission surface. The bridge runs `claude -p --permission-mode dontAsk --setting-sources project` in this directory, so only this file (and managed settings) applies, plus the absolute-path read rules the bridge adds with --settings (bridge.py permission_overlay): anything not allowed is refused without asking, and every Bash call is vetted by ../bash_guard.py. Reads are an ALLOW-LIST: this workspace, the real skill directory and the bot's own oversized command outputs under ~/.claude/projects/<workspace>/<session>/tool-results (both added by the bridge), and the saved triage files. A deny list can't do that job: its `**/.env` style patterns only match under this directory, so a .env anywhere else on the host stayed readable. ~/.claude is not denied wholesale, because a deny beats any allow and would hide those outputs; its config, credentials and transcripts are denied by name instead. bashOutputMaxChars is the documented maximum: an output up to it comes back whole, a bigger one as a preview plus that tool-results file.

hooks.command: python3 "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/../bash_guard.py"; rc=$?; [ $rc -eq 0 ] && exit 0; [ $rc -eq 2 ] || echo 'Blocked: the Bash guard did not run cleanly' >&2; exit 2
